flawed_step: Step 3: Inferring that a unique minimum cut uniquely determines the maximum flow is unjustified. Cut conditions constrain flow across the cut but do not exclude variable circulations on arcs lying within one side.
counterexample: Let V={s,u,v,t}, with arcs s->t, s->u, u->v, v->u, each of capacity 1, and no other arcs. The four s-t cuts {s}, {s,u}, {s,v}, and {s,u,v} have capacities 2, 2, 3, and 1, respectively, so {s,u,v} is the unique minimum cut. Two distinct maximum flows are: (i) f(s->t)=1 and all other arc flows 0; (ii) f(s->t)=1, f(u->v)=f(v->u)=1, and f(s->u)=0. Both have value 1, which is maximum by the cut bound.
assessment_summary: A proof can establish that every maximum flow has value equal to the unique minimum-cut capacity, but it cannot establish uniqueness of the arc-flow assignment. The allowed definition permits circulations, and the displayed four-vertex network has a variable internal circulation while retaining a unique minimum cut.
